authorization.user_statement: 好，我们继续，许可使用Quartus和JTAG来烧写和测试设备。
authorization.scope: Quartus/JTAG volatile FPGA configuration and JTAG-UART device testing

reference_file_input_retry.method: the same Start-Process RedirectStandardInput ordinary-file mechanism as a10-linux-riscv/build/console_tx.ps1

current_run.interpretation: positive control for volatile programming, board clock/power and JTAG-UART target-to-host output only; the no-reset scope did not reach a shell, so this run neither proves nor disproves host-to-target input

historical_input_control.result: same board/cable/tool ordinary-file stdin historically produced command echo, command output and a new vex prompt
historical_input_control.limitation: historical evidence is not substituted for a current golden input run

standard_server_behavior.observation: after a terminal session exits, later nios2-terminal attempts can report no matching JTAG UART even while jtagconfig still sees device 0x02E060DD; waiting 12 minutes did not recover it
standard_server_behavior.classification: second-session enumeration failures are host-server state and are not used as evidence of candidate RTL failure
standard_server_behavior.mitigation_used: only first terminal sessions immediately after a new volatile configuration were treated as output evidence; the server was never stopped or restarted

local_diagnostics.name: registered vendor timing-equivalent bridge probe
local_diagnostics.scope: generated waitrequest phase, registered read_0/RVALID and showahead-OFF FIFO-q timing at the isolated bridge

local_diagnostics.name: exact generated IP control logic with forced RX boundary
local_diagnostics.scope: unmodified Quartus 21.4 generated waitrequest/read_0/rvalid logic plus current bridge; test-only force supplies one RX byte at the FIFO boundary

proved: the corrected synthesis M20K path executes from PC=0 through the complete startup transcript and reaches READY on hardware
the exact T-006 SOF was accepted with the expected checksum and JTAG ID
the candidate JTAG-UART target-to-host path works
three independent host-input mechanisms produced no candidate status/PONG/echo, including the exact historically successful ordinary-file redirection mechanism
not_proved: whether the host byte enters the candidate RX FIFO
whether the candidate CPU pops a byte but observes a stale DATA response
a current golden host-to-target control, because golden did not reach its shell without a forbidden reset action
an RTL defect in the isolated bridge; both local vendor-timing probes pass
classification.next_hypothesis: the missing coverage is full-SoC behavior with the generated IP's registered read timing and a long empty-poll interval before RX injection; only a reproducing test may justify an RTL change

safety_and_resources.final_resource_status: local held by pypto-x/u-ops-registry-batch4; gamepc FREE

blockers: The corrected candidate reaches READY but does not return status/PONG/echo for host input.
Existing focused/behavioral tests do not reproduce the hardware RX failure, and the two added ignored vendor-timing probes pass; changing RTL now would be speculative.
next: Close this board task as partial/blocked and register a separate vendor-faithful full-SoC JTAG-RX reproduction task. If that task proves a defect, implement the minimal RTL fix, rerun affected L0-L2/Gate D/fresh physical/assembler, and repeat volatile board acceptance.
